prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
competitors_mentioned: Board Certification in Personal Injury Trial Law
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” lawyer for every truck-accident case — the right attorney depends on the facts of your case (injuries, fault/coverage issues, whether a commercial carrier or government entity is involved, and whether you need trial experience). I can help you find the best match. To get started, here’s what to look for and what to do next.

What to look for in a Dallas truck-accident lawyer
- Experience with commercial truck cases and federal/state trucking regulations (FMCSA rules, hours-of-service, maintenance and logbooks).  
- Trial experience and a track record of verdicts/large settlements in truck collisions.  
- Access to accident-reconstruction experts, medical specialists and investigators.  
- Board certification in Personal Injury Trial Law (Texas Board of Legal Specialization) is a strong plus.  
- Good client reviews and peer ratings (Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, Super Lawyers).  
- Clear contingency-fee arrangement and transparency about costs and who will handle the file.  
- Local knowledge of Dallas courts and judges.

Where to search and verify credentials
- Texas State Bar attorney search (to confirm license and disciplinary history).  
- Texas Board of Legal Specialization (for board certification).  
- Super Lawyers, Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell for peer and client reviews and profiles.  
- Local bar association referrals (Dallas Bar Association).

Questions to ask during a free consult
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled and what were the outcomes?  
- Have you tried truck cases to verdict? What were the largest recent settlements/verdicts?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day — you or another attorney/associate?  
- Do you have accident-reconstruction and medical experts you use?  
- What is your fee structure and what costs will I be responsible for if we don’t recover?  
- How long do you expect my case to take?  
- Will you handle communications with insurers?

Important timeline note
- In Texas, the statute of limitations for most personal-injury claims is two years from the date of injury — act promptly. (Different rules can apply for claims against government entities.)

If you want, I can:
- Search for highly rated truck-accident attorneys in Dallas and give you a short vetted list with contact info, or  
- Help you evaluate a specific lawyer or firm you’ve found.

Tell me your ZIP code or any details you can share about the crash (date, injuries, whether it involved a commercial truck or government vehicle), and I’ll put together a targeted list.
